## Main outcome

Four distinct eight-whole models were compared over the same four known text
windows. The inherited physical-transformation account no longer has a
protected water/becomes core in this comparison. The exercise does not show
that it is false: it shows concretely why the polished f77r.35 sentence is
insufficient to prefer it. Two independent agents supplied countermodels;

NETWORK independently proposes outlet/its/joins/channel/where/basin and
leaves the last two wholes unknown. Its relation is contact between coexisting
physical endpoints, not a change of substance or physical liquid flow.
MANUAL instead proposes rub/press/stroke/hand/foot/skin/on/it. It leaves much
of the showcase line unknown and tries to explain repeated action sequences
elsewhere. These are different whole-core hypotheses, not eight synonyms for
generic work. Full definitions/debts are in the two agent notes and the
32-row CANDIDATES.tsv, with C0 confidence for every model/whole entry.

## What distinguishes them in the actual selected text

| Source fact | Consequence for the competing accounts |
|---|---|
| f75r.38 AABBA; f76r.52 BAB; f77r.29 AA | MANUAL gives rub-rub-press-press-rub, press-rub-press, rub-rub. This preserves actions but was invented from these known patterns. Others leave the pair unknown; that is missing explanation, not their refutation. |
| f81r.27 ZL/IT chedy.qokedy | MANUAL produces on + imperative press: a concrete local syntactic debt. Do not rescue it by changing press to pressure. Other models do not earn a win by leaving qokedy unknown. |
| f77r.34 qokaiin ... chedy ... qokaiin.qokaiin | Air, pipe, foot and basin all remain repeated. No model may turn the last pair into two objects, both feet, or emphasis without a construction. FLOW also needs a flowing subject: the preceding pipe cannot automatically be it. |
| IT f77r.34 qol.chedy after an earlier chedy | In MANUAL, on-it-on; in NETWORK, joins-there-joins. Both inherit a real extra relation, not an erased word. Root's core-only TRANSFORMATION/FLOW leave qol unknown; full inherited extension retains its prior extra becomes debt. |

| Exact whole | Fixed trial gloss | Scope restriction and principal debt |
|---|---|---|
| qokain | channel? | A bounded passage between places, not the fluid in it. No substring export to qokedy/qolkain. |
| qokaiin | basin? | Container/place, not water, air or an ordinal. Repeated spellings are not automatically different basins. |
| chedy | joins? | Physical contact/connectivity between two referents, not becomes, heats or contains. Binary argument identities remain unproved. |
| solkeey | outlet? | A discharge opening, not vapour. Source and discharge direction unproved. |
| okaiin | its? | Possessive reference, with antecedent unknown. Post-head placement at .35 is an additional grammatical hypothesis. |
| sheedy | where? | Locative linkage, not if, with or a physical condition. Clause and antecedent unknown. |
| qol | there? | Spatial anaphor, not material-from-there or a causal therefore. Location and scope unknown. |
| otedy | inlet? | A receiving opening, not a named liquid or source substance. Direction cannot be read from blue paint. |

All eight are exact-whole C0 inventions selected after seeing the inherited
meanings, images and passage. Some reuse relational intuitions already present
in the route (possession and openings); none is independent lexical evidence.
No historical language, sounding, genre attribution or etymology is proposed.
qokeey, qopchedy, dar, raiin, chedaiin and chealy remain unknown in *this*
rival, not silently redefined or borrowed to finish its sentences.

| Exact source group | Trial gloss | Fixed physical meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `qokeedy` | rub | Move the contacting hand back and forth against a surface. |
| `qokedy` | press | Exert sustained contact force against a surface. |
| `shedy` | stroke | Move the contacting hand along a surface in a single sweep. |
| `qokain` | hand | The anatomical hand. |
| `qokaiin` | foot | The anatomical foot. |
| `qokeey` | skin | The bodily covering. |
| `chedy` | on | Physical surface contact/location, not becomes or contains. |
| `qol` | it | A singular anaphoric referent; antecedent must still be recovered. |

The operational glosses are deliberately different physical movements, not interchangeable “do/process/treat” placeholders. Imperative force is part of the hypothesis, not an independently identified grammatical fact. Anatomical hand is not freely swapped to arm, operator, instrument, or measure; foot is not lower part, base, or unit. Skin is not heat or a preparation. `it` cannot silently become from-it, therefore, or there.

No component inheritance: `okeedy`, `qokeey`, and `qokeedy` are separate; `qolchedy`, `olchedy`, `lchedy`, `solchedy`, and `chedaiin` stay unknown. Bracket alternatives and extended entities stay opaque. In particular, RF `qokee@152;y` is not assigned rub merely because other editions read `qokeedy`.

This is a concrete C0 rival, not a translation or a claim that these are treatment instructions. Its attraction is a coherent inventory of physical operations and contact surfaces across paragraphs. Its weakness is that this inventory was chosen after seeing the patterns, and large portions remain unread. It does not establish eight words, POS, syntax, or a manuscript genre.

Native paragraph flags were separately checked after the coordinator relayed a boundary-audit warning: ZL marks f81r.16–31 as one paragraph; IT ends one at .23 and starts another at .24; RF has no start/end flags throughout this selection. ZL and IT agree on the endpoints of the other three assigned blocks. Thus “complete blocks” describes the supplied selection, not three-edition agreement on paragraph segmentation. The f81r sketch must pay an additional continuity debt across the IT boundary. This metadata audit is not independent semantic evidence, and the relayed correction is an additional exposure; no competing glosses were relayed.
